text: High cardinality alone does not ensure even distribution: frequent shard-key values can bottleneck chunks, while monotonically increasing or decreasing values can concentrate new inserts on the MaxKey or MinKey range. Evaluate value frequency and insert patterns alongside cardinality when selecting a key. (high confidence)

text: Scatter-gather is valid for some workloads: MongoDB documents that it can parallelize large aggregations. Repeated cross-shard requests for routine queries, however, add fan-out and do not scale linearly with shard count. A community discussion records a counterpoint that scatter-gather may help when each shard's working set fits in memory, then challenges whether that benefit survives the extra work as shards are added; evaluate the exception against the actual workload. (high confidence)

text: MongoDB can target a query containing the full shard key or a prefix of a compound shard key to the shard or shards holding the matching data. Queries without shard-key fields are generally broadcast to all shards, so frequent request filters should align with the shard key when query isolation matters. (high confidence)
keywords: Shard key selection for query isolation

text: An ordinary index on a non-shard-key field does not give mongos shard-level query isolation. A predicate that includes the shard key or a compound-key prefix can target the shard or subset that owns matching data; when mongos cannot determine the location from the predicate, it generally broadcasts to all shards. (high confidence)
keywords: Shard key selection for query isolation

text: Choose a key against the dominant query and write workload rather than a convenient field. MongoDB describes the ideal key as one that distributes data evenly and facilitates common query patterns. Percona illustrates the tradeoff with a posts collection whose post_id key isolates single-post reads, even though append writes can concentrate on one shard. AWS gives similar query-frequency, usage-pattern, and cardinality guidance for Amazon DocumentDB Elastic Clusters; that is cross-system support for the selection heuristic, not evidence about MongoDB routing. (high confidence)
keywords: Shard key selection for query isolation

text: Choose a shard key against both common query patterns and distribution needs. MongoDB recommends a key that distributes data evenly while facilitating common query patterns; Percona describes the practical balance as spreading insertions while serving each query from as few shards as possible, ideally one. (high confidence)
keywords: Shard key selection for query isolation

text: Scatter-gather has workload-dependent value: MongoDB says multi-shard requests are less efficient and do not scale linearly as shards are added, while large aggregations can benefit from parallel execution across shards. Even a query containing shard-key fields may still broadcast depending on data distribution and query selectivity. (high confidence)
